construct: Cystathionine beta-synthase normally condenses homocysteine with serine to form cystathionine in the transsulfuration pathway. CBS deficiency causes accumulation of homocysteine and methionine, relative cysteine deficiency, connective-tissue abnormalities, ectopia lentis, and marked thromboembolic risk.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Marfanoid habitus, downward lens dislocation, thrombosis, and elevated homocysteine plus methionine identify classic CBS deficiency, which blocks condensation of homocysteine and serine to cystathionine.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Remethylation defects can raise homocysteine but usually lower methionine; cystathionine gamma-lyase acts downstream; PAH and BCKDH deficiencies produce distinct syndromes. High methionine plus classic phenotype points to CBS.
